evidence: The LC records describe distinct people: n82094233 is Michael Dulany Richards (born 1941), the Sweet Briar historian credited with Europe, 1900-1980 and Twentieth Century Europe; n98023218 is Michael Robert Richards (born 1961), the UWE historian whose A Time of Silence concerns Franco's Spain. These are separate careers, not duplicate authorities.

LC n85044370 identifies Robert M. Taylor Jr. (1941-1999), Indiana Historical Society historian and editor of Generations and Change and The State of Indiana History. LC n78023646 identifies Robert Taylor (born 1943), the Observer labour correspondent and author of The Fifth Estate. The Indiana and British trade-union works belong to different people.

LC n83194224 identifies David Rock (born 1945), author of Argentina, 1516-1982. LC n88010583 identifies David Rock (born 20 August 1946), lecturer in German at Keele and author/editor of Voices in Times of Change and Jurek Becker. The Argentine historian and German-literature scholar are distinct people.

a mixes David F. Smith's nutrition history (LC n96034774, born 1954) with a 1911 article and unrelated studies. b's Cromwell books belong to David Lawrence Smith (LC n90672438, born 1963); its Paradoxes of Dehumanization is by David Livingstone Smith. The LC authorities describe different people, and the supplied works contain additional namesakes.

a combines the Newcastle political philosopher's Human Rights, Group Rights, and Peoples' Rights with welfare historian Peter Jones's Voices from the Far North. Its Q91110948/ORCID anchor instead identifies medieval-medicine scholar Peter Murray Jones. b's Q20127892/LC n90703306 identifies Peter Michael Jones (born 1949), the Birmingham historian of France. These anchors and works do not describe one person.

a is principally phenomenologist David Tredway Carr (LC n83222092, born 1940), author of Time, Narrative, and History, but includes the gratitude volume edited by Birmingham education philosopher David Carr. b is biblical scholar David McLain Carr (LC n91083963, born 1961), author of Reading the Fractures of Genesis. The LC authorities are distinct, and a includes another namesake's work.

a combines Lancaster oral historian Elizabeth Mauchline Roberts's A Woman's Place and Women and Families (LC n84016771, born 1936) with Michigan anthropologist Elizabeth F. S. Roberts's Assisted Existence. b's LC n92029155 identifies Elizabeth Roberts (born 1944), a writer on Russian affairs credited with Georgia, Armenia, and Azerbaijan. The authorities are distinct and a conflates authors.

The LC authorities are distinct: n79041833 identifies William B. Taylor (born 1943), author of Landlord and Peasant in Colonial Oaxaca; n93075913 identifies William Banks Taylor (born 1944), author of Brokered Justice. a additionally contains the 1844 Narrative of the Texan Santa Fe Expedition, which is George Wilkins Kendall's work, so its works are mixed rather than one clean author bibliography.

LC n95027424 identifies Robert Stein (born 17 June 1960), Leiden historian and author of Politiek en historiografie, consistent with the Burgundian Netherlands books. LC n79096632 identifies Robert Louis Stein (born 2 January 1948), Toronto historian and author of The French Slave Trade and The French Sugar Business. The records describe different people and separate bodies of work.

LC n88058532 identifies Michael Warner (born 9 September 1958), the English scholar credited with The Origins of Literary Studies in America, matching the public-sphere and queer-theory books. LC n95036430 identifies Michael Warner (born 28 August 1960) of the CIA History Staff, credited with The CIA under Harry Truman and Changing Witness. These are distinct authorities for different people.

a spans publications from 1881 to 2002 and includes The Trials of Thomas Bylney, which the publisher credits to John F. Davis; it cannot represent one career. b's LC n97010723 identifies John Richard Davis (born 30 January 1965), author of Britain and the German Zollverein. The mixed generic key cannot safely be merged with this historian of Anglo-German relations.

a mixes J. C. D. Clark's British political and religious history with Bugs in the System, credited to J. F. Clark, and classical/archaeological papers. b lists the unrelated modern US Army book Preparing for War; its LC no00069526 actually describes J. P. Clark as the recorder of Thomas Anderson's account, not a verified authority for that modern author. Neither key supports a person-level merge.

a's Confederation thesis/book and business-history works belong to Andrew Smith (LC nb2008020191, born 1976), but Reading against the Postcolonial Grain is listed by Glasgow sociologist Andrew Smith, whose ORCID differs. b's LC no89019638 identifies Andrew Franklin Smith (born 1946), author of The Tomato in America and the food histories. The LC authorities describe different people, and a includes a third namesake.

LC nr92021749 identifies photographer Robert Holden Dawson (born 19 August 1950), explicitly credited with Farewell, Promised Land and A Doubtful River. LC n88075278 identifies Canadian political scientist Robert MacGregor Dawson (1895-1958), whose Government of Canada appeared before the photographer was born. The authorities describe different people; the later government-book editions do not extend Dawson's lifespan.

LC n50044504 identifies Hugh Edward Richardson (1905-2000), diplomat and Tibetologist credited with Tibet and Its History. LC n83171556 identifies Henry Gerald Richardson (1884-1974), author of The English Jewry under Angevin Kings and The English Parliament in the Middle Ages. The Tibetan-history and medieval British legal-history works belong to distinct people, not duplicate authorities.
